page: UpCloud STARTER-1xCPU-2GB is an entry-level virtual server configured with 1 shared vCPU, 2.0 GB of RAM, and 20 GB of local SSD storage. Hosted on KVM virtualization, the instance utilizes an AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The single assigned core features a 64 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a 16 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions. The instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations illustrate strong single-threaded processing alongside lower aggregate throughput dictated by the single-vCPU ceiling. In stress-ng single-core execution, the instance achieved a score of 3751.37, placing it in the top tier of tested hardware. Compression and decompression benchmarks reflect similar single-core efficiency, with single-threaded gzip compression registering 39.04 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression recording 17.41 GB/sec. Conversely, the overall multi-core stress-ng score matches the single-core score at 3751.37, ranking in the lower quartile across all systems. Large block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 34.26 GB/sec, while write operations measured 31.63 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 3.49 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 5.44 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Due to its shared single-core design and constrained 2.0 GB memory envelope, the instance presents low operational resource costs geared toward lightweight, non-parallel computational demands. It delivers efficient instruction execution on isolated single-threaded tasks, but capacity is restricted for multi-threaded services, large in-memory databases, or parallel compiling. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, lightweight automation scripts, low-traffic API endpoints, small development environments, and microservices with minimal concurrency requirements.

However, overall system throughput is limited by its single-core capacity and 2.0 GB RAM footprint, resulting in lower-quartile multi-core and memory benchmark scores. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not contain a GPU. The instance provides economical resource utilization for lightweight applications, microservices, development testing, small utility jobs, and low-traffic web serving where multi-threaded scale is not required.
